To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combinatorial delivery of different inhibitors with different activities on glioma cells, angiogenesis, and migration leads to a prolonged and increased glioma growth inhibition.
the combinatorial use of inhibitors of glioma angiogenesis with inhibitors of glioma invasion produces a more prolonged and increased inhibition on glioma growth.

the combinatorial delivery of molecules that simultaneously inhibit glioma angiogenesis (e.g., PEX and PF4/CTF) or glioma invasion (e.g., PF-4/CTP, PF-4/DR, or PEX), leads to a prolonged inhibition of the tumor growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of new drugs for the treatment of malignant glioma and the design of combinatorial strategies for the administration of these drugs.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies to treat brain tumors, which have been largely unsuccessful in recent years.
the development of a new therapeutic approach for malignant gliomas, based on the combined administration of different inhibitors affecting both glioma and tumor angiogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combinatorial approach of different molecules that affect glioma growth by different mechanisms, such as angiogenesis and invasion, can lead to a prolonged and increased therapeutic effect in mouse glioma models.

the combinatorial delivery of molecules targeting both tumor angiogenesis and invasion is more effective in the control of malignant gliomas than the delivery of molecules that act on tumor angiogenesis only.
the combination of molecules that affect both tumor and endothelium by different mechanisms can lead to an enhanced inhibition of glioma angiogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a combination of inhibitors with different mechanisms of action can produce a prolonged inhibition and a strong therapeutic effect on glioma growth.
combinatorial therapy is more effective than monotherapy and that it should be used to treat gliomas.
combinatorial administration is a powerful tool to increase the efficacy of glioma-targeted therapies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to achieve prolonged inhibition of glioblastoma growth by using inhibitors targeting both angiogenesis and tumor migration.
combining different inhibitors that act on glioma angiogen- esis and invasion may lead to a more effective treatment.
it is possible to combine molecules that act on both tumor and endothelium cells and that these combinations can be more effective than single molecules.
